plants.description: Evergreen Andean foothill tree with reddish bark and paired glossy leaves. Bark is bitter and fibrous when peeled in strips.
plants.uses: Bark yields quinine — the classic fever remedy of the basin outposts. Field medics steep thin shavings in hot water for malaria fever.

plants.description: Woody climbing vine of the understory. Bright red fruit capsules split to show a black seed with a white aril — like a watching eye.
plants.uses: Seeds roasted and ground into a stimulating paste or drink. Used for long night watches and to blunt river fever fatigue.

plants.description: Tall canopy tree with trifoliate leaves and milky latex that beads white when the bark is cut.
plants.uses: Latex collected for waterproofing kit, boot repairs, and sealing radio crates against humidity. Smoke-cured sheets keep longer in the wet.

plants.description: Slender multi-stem palm of floodplain forest. Dark purple berry clusters hang below feathery fronds.
plants.uses: Fruit pulp is a dense riverside staple — energy food for paddlers. Leaves and stems also used for temporary thatch and baskets.

plants.description: Large hardwood with compound leaves. A clear golden oleoresin can be tapped from the trunk.
plants.uses: Resin used as a wound balm and lamp oil extender. Local boatmen rub it on cuts that refuse to dry in the wet season.

plants.description: Low shade herb of moist forest floor. Knobby roots and small paired leaves hug the leaf litter.
plants.uses: Root preparations historically used to clear the gut of toxins and as an expectorant. Dose carefully — strong medicine.
